solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Corpulent celebrities I caught having a resigned attitude

parts.note: corpulent means fat
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone overweight, surrounded by stars, feels resigned to their lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts run in clue order: FAT + A-LIST + I + C gives FATALISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes outcomes are fixed in advance, so their outlook is one of passive acceptance.

clue.text: A qualification for doctor catching one bug

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: a doctorate, the degree that makes someone a doctor
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor's diploma, with a bug caught somewhere along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A PhD is the academic doctorate; I slips inside it, after A: A + PH(I)D.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect such as a greenfly, and bug is a loose everyday word for any insect.

clue.text: Cause of lapses and bad manners vicar periodically ignored

indicators.note: skipping letters at regular intervals leaves every other one standing

parts.note: the even letters of these three words run together, the odd ones dropped

explanation.surface: A rude vicar whose behaviour causes lapses in etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the letter string: bAdMaNnErSvIcAr leaves AMNESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, which produces gaps or lapses in what a person can recall.

clue.text: Climber coming from peaks of inactive volcanoes? Yes!

indicators.note: a peak is the top, and in a down clue the top of each word is its first letter

parts.note: initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a mountaineer started from the summits of dormant volcanoes, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, fitting the volcano scene, but it means a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is an evergreen plant that grows up walls and trees, so it is a classic climbing plant.

clue.text: Maybe saw manufacturer talk more foolishly about nothing

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
doing something foolishly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone babbles ever more foolishly about nothing at all, perhaps a saw manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: TALK MORE rearranges to TOLMAKER, which then goes around O to give TOOLMAKER. 'Maybe' flags a saw as one example of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one kind of tool, so a firm making saws is an example of a tool manufacturer.

clue.text: Complaint made by Conservative greeting Liberal Left

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Conservative
hi is an informal greeting
standard abbreviation for Liberal
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political grumble from a Tory saying hello to a left-wing Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance in this political scene, but it is the medical sense: an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a complaint is an illness, and a chill is a mild feverish cold caught from the cold.

clue.text: Classical sextet and former queen turned up in capital

parts.note: six in Roman, that is classical, numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something upward makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned in Britain in the early 1700s

explanation.surface: A group of six classical musicians and an old queen appear in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical sextet' suggests chamber music, fitting the city, but it means Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, fittingly famed for its classical music.

clue.text: Farm worker tucked into sherry, gutted to get diluted alcohol

indicators.note: being tucked into something means sitting inside it
gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a farmhand is a worker on a farm

explanation.surface: A labourer downs sherry, feels wretched, and switches to a weaker drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it empties sherry to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, so its alcohol content is watered down.

clue.text: Some euros I risked for powerful underworld figure

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Gambling some euros on a deal with a mob boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a gangster, but here it is the mythological land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian god who rules the realm of the dead and judges souls there.

clue.text: Love of the French lyrical compositions

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O
des is French for 'of the' before a plural

explanation.surface: A French love of songs and poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as zero comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often addressed to a subject in an elevated style.

clue.text: Mark humiliating Cockney speaking unclearly

indicators.note: the London Cockney accent famously drops the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
humbling means humiliating

explanation.surface: A Cockney named Mark, embarrassed, can't get his words out clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but stands for M. Cockney speech drops H, so humbling becomes 'umbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumble is to say words indistinctly with the mouth partly closed, so a mumbler is hard to understand.

clue.text: Assessment of vehicle with current tax Edward's driven

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
I is the physics symbol for electric current
value added tax, the UK sales tax
Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward's car has passed its test and its road tax is up to date, so he can drive it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driven' sounds like motoring, but it means ambitious. The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety test; VAT is its sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A driven person is pushed on by strong ambition or determination, which is what being highly motivated means.

clue.text: Begin touring upper-class, royal house

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling all round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: begin means start
U is the abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: Starting a tour of a grand, royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal house' suggests a palace building, but it means a dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were a dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England, so they are a royal family line.

clue.text: 100 withdrawn from account, possibly? One has a large bill

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered
withdrawing something takes it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a hundred out of the bank, maybe to pay someone's big bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one C from ACCOUNT and rearrange what is left. 'Bill' reads as an invoice, fitting the banking scene, but it is a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A toucan is a tropical bird known for its huge, brightly coloured beak, and bill is another word for beak.

clue.text: One US state or another which doesn't have a river

indicators.note: lacking something means it has been removed

parts.note: another US state
A taken as written, R the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Naming a US state, or another one that has no river.
explanation.walkthrough: The other state is Arkansas; take A and R from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a state in the American Midwest, so it is simply one of the fifty.

clue.text: More agile African runner goes round doctor on run

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: a river is a runner, and the Nile is Africa's best known
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A faster African athlete laps a doctor who is jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African runner' suggests an athlete, but a runner here is a river: the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble means quick and light in movement, so the comparative describes someone with greater agility.

clue.text: Baker might make this business revenue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastry folded over a fruit filling
second meaning: the total sales a company takes in a period

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a definition by example, describing what comes out of a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple turnover is a folded pastry from a bakery; separately, a firm's annual sales figure is called its turnover.

clue.text: Well-known chemist in front of Boots during festive season

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A famous pharmacist standing outside Boots at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British high-street pharmacy chain, which the chemist suggests; here only its B is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and founded the Nobel prizes.

clue.text: Reveal posterior part of gizmo, once

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Showing the back end of some gadget from the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posterior' reads as an adjective meaning rear, fitting the gadget, but it is a noun: the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is slang for baring one's buttocks at someone as a prank or insult.

clue.text: Wrong party for Trump

parts.note: out can mean mistaken, as in a calculation being out
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: The wrong political party for Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician, fitting 'party', but it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump someone is to beat them, as a trump card beats other cards, which is to surpass them.

clue.text: Grandmaster capturing a piece in sacrificial stratagem

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner and holding, so one part is enclosed by another

parts.note: GM is the chess title abbreviation
taken as written
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A chess grandmaster takes a piece as part of a sacrificial opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capturing a piece' sounds like chess, but only A goes inside GM; the piece is a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is a chess opening in which a pawn is given up for advantage, hence any calculated sacrificial ploy.

clue.text: Literature penned by Gothic writer giving no offence

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in an animal pen, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote Gothic horror tales
lit is short for literature

explanation.surface: A Gothic author writing material that offends no one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like 'written', fitting the writer, but here it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being polite means being courteous and well mannered, so behaving in a way unlikely to upset anyone.

clue.text: Pastry that is after prawns for starters

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter of the word
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Pastry is the course served after the prawn starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places IE behind P. 'For starters' sounds like a menu course, but it takes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish in a pastry case, so pastry stands in for it loosely.

clue.text: Working loom raised for convenience

indicators.note: something working is in operation, its parts moving and changing places

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A loom in operation is lifted up to make it easier to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convenience' reads as ease of use, but in Britain a public convenience is a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' room is a women's toilet, and convenience is the British euphemism for a lavatory.
